p.src: Now Sun Wukong and the other two followed the summoning official to the Meridian Gate, where a chamberlain immediately reported their arrival and received orders to admit them. The three stood there together without bowing. The king asked, “Are you three the eminent disciples of the holy monk, our imperial son-in-law? What are your surnames and names? Where do you live? Why did you enter the religious life? And what scriptures are you going to obtain?” Wukong immediately stepped forward, intending to mount the hall. A guard beside him shouted, “Do not advance! Whatever you have to say, stand there and report it.” Wukong laughed. “We who have left the world advance whenever we gain a step.” Bajie and Sha Monk then came forward as well. Fearing that their rustic manners might alarm the sovereign, the elder rose and called, “Disciples, His Majesty has asked why you came. Report it to him.” Seeing his master standing in attendance at the side, Wukong could not restrain himself and cried aloud, “Your Majesty belittles others and thereby belittles yourself. Since you have chosen my master as your imperial son-in-law, why make him stand in attendance? In this world a princess’s husband is called an honored person. How can an honored person be left without a seat?” At this the king turned pale with shock. He wanted to withdraw from the hall, but feared losing dignity before the court. He had no choice but to summon his courage and order an attendant to bring an embroidered stool, upon which he invited the Tang Monk to sit. Only then did Wukong make his report:

p.src: Hearing this, the king was at once greatly alarmed and greatly delighted: delighted that his daughter had taken a living Buddha for her husband, and alarmed that the three disciples were indeed monstrous divinities. While he wavered between alarm and delight, the court astrologer suddenly reported, “The wedding date has been fixed for the twelfth day of this month in the present year, at the auspicious renzi hour. All the directional omens are favorable, and it is fitting to solemnize the marriage.” The king asked, “What is today’s date?” The astrologer reported, “Today is the eighth, the day of wushen. The monkey offers fruit; it is an excellent day to welcome worthies and undertake affairs.” Overjoyed, the king immediately ordered the officers in attendance to clean the halls, pavilions, towers, and terraces of the imperial garden. He invited his son-in-law and the three disciples to rest there while preparations were made for the fine wedding feast and the princess’s marriage. All respectfully obeyed. The king withdrew from court, and the assembled officials dispersed; of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now Sanzang and his disciples all went to the imperial garden. As evening gradually fell, a vegetarian meal was set out. Bajie said happily, “At last it is time we had something to eat today.” The stewards brought shoulder-load after shoulder-load of plain rice, noodles, and other vegetarian foods. Bajie ate and asked for more, then ate the refills and asked again, stopping only when his belly was stretched to bursting. Presently lamps were lit and bedding laid out, and each retired to sleep.

p.src: When the elder saw that no one else was near, he angrily reproached Wukong, crying, “Wukong, you wretched macaque, time and again you bring disaster upon me! I told you that we should merely go and have our travel document exchanged, and not approach the festooned tower. Why did you insist on leading me there to look? A fine sight it has proved! Now we have brought this whole affair upon ourselves. What are we to do?” Wukong smiled appeasingly. “Master, you said, ‘My late mother also threw an embroidered ball, met a destined partner from former lives, and became his wife.’ You seemed to admire that ancient custom, so I led you there. I also remembered what the elder of the Gold-Spreading Monastery of the Solitary One had told us and wished to test whether it was true. When I saw the emperor just now, his face bore a faint shadow of ill fortune. Only we have yet to see what the princess is like.” The elder asked, “And what will you do once you see the princess?” Wukong replied, “With my fiery eyes and golden pupils, a single look at a face tells me truth from falsehood, good from evil, wealth from poverty. Then I shall know how to act and distinguish the wicked from the righteous.” Sha Monk and Bajie laughed. “Our elder brother has lately learned physiognomy too!” Wukong said, “Professional physiognomists are fit to be my grandsons.” Sanzang shouted, “Enough of your banter! He is now determined to take me as his son-in-law. Just how are we to deal with this?” Wukong replied, “At the wedding celebration on the twelfth, the princess will surely come out to pay her respects to her parents. I shall watch her from the side. If she truly is a woman, you may as well become the imperial son-in-law and enjoy all the splendor and wealth of this kingdom.” At these words Sanzang grew even angrier and cursed him: “You vile macaque! You are still trying to ruin me! As Wuneng said, we have already climbed nine full sections and seven or eight tenths of the tenth, yet you still prod me with that glib tongue of yours. Hold it at once, and do not open that foul mouth of yours. If you show such insolence again, I shall recite the spell and leave you unable to bear it.” Hearing him threaten to recite the spell, Wukong hastily knelt before him and said, “Do not recite it! Do not recite it! If she really is a woman, then when it is time to bow at the wedding, we shall all raise havoc in the palace and take you away.”

p.src: After all the civil and military officials had completed their audience, the king proclaimed, “Let the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepare a splendid wedding banquet for the twelfth. For today, prepare spring wine and invite the imperial son-in-law to enjoy himself in the imperial garden.” He ordered the Office of Ceremonies to escort the three honored kinsmen to rest awhile at the Hall of Foreign Envoys, and the Court of Imperial Entertainments to prepare three vegetarian tables there for their reception. At both places the Music Office was to perform, attending them as they admired the spring scenery and passed the long day. When Bajie heard this, he immediately called out, “Your Majesty, we master and disciples have remained together ever since we met and have never been separated for even a moment. Since there is to be a banquet in the imperial garden today, take us along to enjoy ourselves for a couple of days, and then our master can become your family’s son-in-law. Otherwise, this bargain will come to nothing.” The king saw how ugly he was and heard his coarse speech; moreover, Bajie kept twisting his head and neck, thrusting out his snout, and wagging his ears, as though half-mad. Fearing that he might spoil the marriage, the king had no choice but to consent. He ordered, “Set two tables in the Pavilion of Eternal Pacification of China and the Barbarians, where I shall sit with my son-in-law. Set three tables in the Pavilion for Detaining Spring and invite the three gentlemen to sit separately, lest the order of seating prove awkward between master and disciples.” Only then did the fool make a salute toward the throne and call, “Many thanks!” They each withdrew. The king also issued an edict ordering the palace officials to arrange a banquet. The empresses and consorts of the inner palaces were to dress the princess’s hair and add to her trousseau, in preparation for the auspicious marriage on the twelfth.

p.src: Wukong and the other two likewise enjoyed every comfort in the Pavilion of Lingering Spring. Each drank several cups, and all were somewhat tipsy. Just as they were about to look for the elder, they saw that he was already in a pavilion with the king. Bajie’s foolish nature asserted itself, and he called out at once, “What pleasure, what ease! Today we have finally had a taste of fine living. Now that we are full, we ought to go to sleep.” Sha Monk laughed. “Second Brother, you truly have no self-discipline. How can you sleep when you are so stuffed and bloated?” Bajie said, “What do you know? The common saying goes, ‘If you do not lie stiff after eating, you have no slab of fat in your belly.’”

p.src: Tripitaka took leave of the king and came into the pavilion, where he angrily rebuked Bajie: “You clod! You grow more boorish by the day. What kind of place do you think this is, that you keep shouting at the top of your voice? If you should anger the king, would he not have our lives taken?” Bajie said, “Nothing will happen, nothing will happen. We are related to him by marriage, so he cannot very well take offense. As the saying goes, ‘Kinship cannot be broken by blows, nor neighborliness by curses.’ We are all just having fun. Why should we fear him?” The elder barked an order to bring the fool over and give him twenty strokes of the monk’s staff. Wukong promptly seized him and threw him down, and the elder raised his staff to strike. The fool cried out, “Mercy, Lord Imperial Son-in-law! Forgive me, forgive me!” The banquet officials nearby intervened and stopped them. The fool scrambled up and muttered under his breath, “What a great dignitary, what an imperial son-in-law! The marriage is not even made, and already he is enforcing the royal law.” Wukong covered his mouth and said, “Do not talk nonsense. Stop talking nonsense and hurry off to bed.”

p.src: Before they knew it, three or four days of merriment had passed, and the auspicious twelfth day arrived. Officials from the three departments of the Court of Imperial Entertainments reported, “Your servants received the decree on the eighth. The imperial son-in-law’s residence is now complete and awaits only the arrangement of the bridal trousseau. The wedding banquet is also fully prepared, with more than five hundred meat and vegetarian tables in all.” The king was delighted and was about to invite his son-in-law to the feast when a palace official suddenly reported before the throne, “Your Majesty, the principal queen requests your presence.” The king therefore withdrew into the inner palace, where he found the three palace queens and the consorts of the six courts leading the princess, all chatting and laughing in the Palace of Radiant Sun. It was truly a mass of blossoms and brocade, a scene of sumptuous and enchanting splendor that surpassed the moon palace of heaven and yielded nothing to the jade halls of the immortals. Four new verses on Joy, Gathering, Felicity, and Marriage bear witness to the scene.

p.src: Now when the king arrived, the queens and consorts led the princess, together with the court ladies and palace maids, out to welcome him. Beaming with joy, the king entered the Palace of Radiant Sun and took his seat. After the queens and consorts had paid homage, the king said, “My worthy daughter, since you hung the decorations and cast the embroidered ball on the eighth, you have had the good fortune to encounter the holy monk, and I imagine your heart’s desire is now fulfilled. The officials of every bureau have also understood Our wishes, and all arrangements are complete. Today is the appointed day. You should attend the wedding banquet early and not miss the auspicious hour.” The princess stepped forward, prostrated herself, and reported, “Father King, I beg you to pardon your daughter’s countless offenses and permit me to say one thing. In recent days I have heard palace officials say that the holy monk of the Tang has three disciples, all exceedingly ugly and fearsome in appearance. Your daughter dares not see them, for I fear that the sight of them would surely terrify me. I earnestly beg Father King to send them out of the city. That would spare my frail body from fright and injury and prevent a calamity instead.” The king said, “Had you not mentioned it, child, We would almost have forgotten. They are indeed somewhat ugly. For the past few days I have had them entertained in the Pavilion of Lingering Spring in the imperial garden. We shall go to court today, endorse their travel document, and send them out of the city. Then the banquet may proceed properly.” The princess kowtowed and thanked him for his favor. The king immediately proceeded to the throne hall and issued a decree summoning his son-in-law and the other three.

They are indeed somewhat ugly. For the past few days I have had them entertained in the Pavilion of Lingering Spring in the imperial garden.
We shall go to court today, endorse their travel document, and send them out of the city. Then the banquet may proceed properly.”
The princess kowtowed and thanked him for his favor.
The king immediately proceeded to the throne hall and issued a decree summoning his son-in-law and the other three.

p.src: As it happened, Tripitaka had been counting the days on his fingers. Having endured until the twelfth, before dawn he consulted the three disciples: “Today is already the twelfth. How are we to handle this affair?” Wukong said, “I have already perceived a touch of ill fortune about that king, but it has not yet fastened upon him, so there is no great danger. The only trouble is that we have not been able to see the princess. If she comes out, one glance from me will reveal whether she is genuine or false, and only then can we act. You need only set your mind at ease. They are certain to summon us now and send the rest of us out of the city. Simply agree and do not be afraid. I shall slip away and return at once, remaining close beside you to protect you.”

p.src: While master and disciples were still talking, they indeed saw the royal equerry arrive with officials from the Office of Ceremonial Regulations to summon them. Wukong laughed and said, “Let us go, let us go. They must be preparing to send us on our way so that they may keep Master here for the marriage.” Bajie said, “For our farewell they are bound to give us a thousand or more taels of gold and silver. Then we can buy some gifts to take home. When we reach my father-in-law’s house, I can visit my kin and enjoy myself again.” Sha Monk said, “Second Brother, clamp your mouth shut and stop talking nonsense. We shall follow whatever Eldest Brother decides.”

p.src: They therefore took their luggage and horse and followed the officials to the foot of the vermilion steps. When the king saw them, he ordered Wukong and the other two to approach and said, “Bring up your travel document. We shall affix Our seal and signature and return it to you. We shall also provide ample journey money so that you three may promptly go to Spirit Mountain and see the Buddha. If you return after obtaining the scriptures, We shall reward you handsomely again. Your imperial son-in-law will remain here, so you need not worry about him.” Wukong expressed his thanks. He then told Sha Monk to take out the travel document and hand it up. After looking it over, the king affixed his seal and signature. He also brought out ten ingots of gold and twenty of silver as a modest token of regard between relations. Bajie had always been strongly attached to wealth and women, so he immediately went forward and accepted them. Facing the throne, Wukong made a respectful bow and said, “We have troubled you, we have troubled you.” Then he turned to leave. Tripitaka was so alarmed that he scrambled to his feet, grabbed Wukong, and said through clenched teeth, “Are all of you leaving without any concern for me?” Wukong squeezed Tripitaka’s palm, gave him a meaningful look, and said, “Stay here, put your mind at ease, and enjoy your wedding. When we have obtained the scriptures, we shall return to visit you.” The elder half believed him and half did not, and refused to release his hand. All the officials saw this and believed that they were truly parting from one another. Presently the king again invited his son-in-law into the throne hall and ordered the assembled officials to escort the other three out of the city. The elder had no choice but to release Wukong’s hand and ascend to the throne hall.

p.src: The Pilgrim and his two companions left the court together with the others, then took their separate ways. Pigsy said, “Are we really leaving?” The Pilgrim said nothing and walked straight back to the posthouse. The posthouse master welcomed them inside, served tea, and laid out a meal. The Pilgrim said to Pigsy and Sandy, “You two stay here and be sure not to show yourselves. Whatever the posthouse master asks, give him vague answers for the time being, and do not speak to me. I am going to protect Master.”

His true body, meanwhile, sprang into midair with a twist and changed into a little honeybee. And this is what was seen:

p.src: See how he flew lightly into the court. From afar he saw Tripitaka seated on an embroidered stool to the king’s left, his brows knitted with sorrow and his heart consumed by anxiety. He flew straight onto Tripitaka’s Vairocana cap, quietly crawled to his ear, and called, “Master, I am here. Do not worry.” Only Tripitaka heard these words; none of those ordinary mortals could possibly perceive them. When Tripitaka heard him, his heart at last grew easier. Before long, a palace official came to announce, “Your Majesty, the wedding feast has been prepared in Zhiques Palace. Her Majesty and the princess are both waiting there and respectfully invite Your Majesty and the honored guest to join the marriage celebration.” The king was overjoyed and immediately entered the inner palace with his imperial son-in-law. Indeed:
